pairs.subject: quality-gates
pairs.evidence: lib/db/readiness.ts:126 The readiness gate (which every public loader passes through and which the /data release gate reuses) refuses with only what failed, e.g. `contract 0<100000`, and names no remedy. It also leaves the file's own prose rule about floors unmechanised and offers a blanket env bypass.

techniques.evidence: lib/db/readiness.ts:126 The refusal says what is below its floor but gives no remedy (re-ingest, restore a snapshot, or which pass grew the corpus), so the operator reading /admin or the log has nothing to run.

lib/db/readiness.ts:42 The rule 'floor ≈65–72 % of corpus; raise it in the change that grows the corpus' exists only as a comment. floorVerdicts (line 77) checks only count >= floor, even though it holds both numbers. The one test (features/data-releases/manifest.test.ts) pins only `contract` against a hard-coded corpus literal, so a floor left two orders of magnitude low on any other kind stays green, which is the very failure the comment records.

lib/db/readiness.ts:100 The escape hatch is an unnamed blanket: one env token waives every floor kind for the whole process instead of naming the kind or finding it waives. It is logged once, but its reach is everything.
lib/db/readiness.test.ts:35 A seeded known violation (floor−1 rows) is shown to turn the gate red, and the empty store is asserted not ready (line 22).
lib/db/readiness.ts:76 A kind missing from the counts fails closed (counted as 0) instead of sailing past the floor, and the doc comment says an empty store fails loudly.

lib/db/storeSource.test.ts:32 The absence assertion on line 31 is paired with this presence assertion over the same file, and line 23 asserts the extracted population is non-empty before comparing counts.

pairs.subject: quality-gates
pairs.evidence: features/civicscore/duelParam.test.ts:157 The source guard that says the duel address is built only through duelAddress() searches raw source text, and the hook's header comment (features/civicscore/useDuelSelection.ts:28, "`duelAddress()`") already contains that string, so the presence check would stay green with every real call removed.

techniques.evidence: features/civicscore/duelParam.test.ts:157 The haystack is not reduced to what executes, and a comment satisfies the presence assertion. The same file knew this hazard for the import check (line 137) and for '?souboj=' (lines 153-156) but did not apply it here. lensDuelSource.test.ts:16 also asserts presence over raw source.
features/civicscore/verdictRung.test.ts:38 The instrument is asserted before the result: each surface must yield at least 3 badge sites, so the per-site loop cannot pass vacuously over zero matches.

features/civicscore/scoreClaim.ts:76 The required review field gets a distinct third value for a deterministic recomputation instead of a judgment-shaped shrug like pending review (rationale at lines 21-23).

pairs.subject: quality-gates
pairs.evidence: components/MpProfileBeacon.tsx:4 The context is two client components: an analytics beacon and a locale toggle.
